plan: [ This is effectively a second-price auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest (the exit price when the second bidder drops). With i.i.d. private values and risk-neutral preferences, bidding truthfully is a dominant strategy. Overbidding risks winning at a price above my value; underbidding risks losing when I should profit. There’s only one round, so no strategic signaling or learning applies. I will bid my value of $24 to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This is effectively a second‑price auction via an ascending clock: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your value. Overbidding risks negative payoff if you win above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With only one round and uniform values, no learning advantage exists. Bid truthfully at 16.0. ]

[ This mechanism is equivalent to a second‑price auction: the ascending clock with exit at sealed bid makes the winner pay the highest competing bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy is to bid truthfully. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks winning at a price above value. My value is 24, so I set my sealed bid/exit price to 24 to maximize expected profit this round. Ties, if any, are random and do not change the optimality of truth-telling. ]
